HIV infection was associated with a slower hematological response in a population living with high HIV and malaria prevalence in Zambia.
HIV-1-infested individuals have a slower hematological reconstitution after malaria than HIV-1 un-infected patients.
HIV-infected malaria patients have slower hematological recovery, and that malaria preventive measures should be specifically targeted to this high risk group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of HIV infection on the hematological response to malaria treatment.
the effect of malaria on hematological recovery in HIV-1-inflected and uninfected patients.
the impact of HIV infection on the hematological response to antimalarial treatment in a population where malaria and HIV are highly prevalent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
malaria and HIV infection have a synergistic effect on hematologic recovery.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-infected patients have a slower hematological improvement after malaria infection.
HIV-1 infection has a significant negative impact on hematological recovery after clinical malaria.
HIV-1-infested patients with malaria have a slower hematological response to antimalarial treatment and a slower recovery from the anemia caused by malaria than noninfected patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV-1-infested malaria patients have a slower hematological response after successful parasite clearance, which could be a consequence of a more severe malaria infection and/or a more severe anemia.

HIV-1-inflected individuals who develop malaria have a much more severe anemia than those who do not.
